title: U.S. House · Arizona's 5th District
area: East Valley suburbs of Phoenix, including parts of Mesa, Gilbert, Queen Creek, San Tan Valley, and Apache Junction.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Republican Andy Biggs, who had held the seat since 2017, did not seek re-election and instead ran for governor of Arizona. Elizabeth Lee won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.5% of the vote over Chris James and Brian Hualde. Mark Lamb, the former Pinal County Sheriff (2017-2024) and 2024 U.S. Senate candidate, won the Republican primary with 58.6% over self-funded businessman Daniel Keenan, defeating candidates including state legislators Travis Grantham and Mike Gross for the nomination; Andy Biggs also withdrew from this primary. Lamb's primary win came amid public allegations from multiple women, reported by the Arizona Republic and KTAR News, that he had sent them sexually charged messages and, in one case, threatened revenge-porn charges; Lamb did not deny specific claims but called many of them baseless, and a Pinal County Attorney's Office review found no evidence of criminal conduct. Cook Political Report rated the district R+10.

candidates.name: Elizabeth Lee
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 64.5% of the vote

summary.text: Elizabeth Lee is a registered nurse, board-certified reproductive health and infertility nurse, and patient advocate, running as the Democratic nominee to become the first woman to represent Arizona's 5th Congressional District. She has been affiliated with reproductive-health and healthcare-advocacy organizations including the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and RESOLVE: The National Infertility Association.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Dover High School, a bachelor's degree from Northwestern State University in 2005, and an associate degree from the Carrington College of Nursing in 2013.

Career experience includes working as a nurse, consultant, and healthcare advocate; has been affiliated with the American Society for Reproductive Medicine, the ASRM Center for Policy Leadership, the Pacific Coast Reproductive Society, Reproductive Freedom for All, RESOLVE: The National Infertility Association, and the Arizona State Board of Nursing.
Says she grew up battling an undiagnosed illness for years, which she says shaped her decision to become a nurse and patient advocate.
background.quote: I grew up battling a mysterious illness that went undiagnosed for years, and it was only after becoming a nurse that I began to crack my own medical mystery.

background.text: Endorsed by Rep. Adelita Grijalva (D), state Sen. Analise Ortiz (D), and Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes (D), among other groups.

priorities.text: Healthcare as a human right, citing her nursing background and work with families facing infertility and other medical crises, pledging to fight so 'no one is left behind, no child denied care and no family bankrupted for the right to live.'
priorities.quote: In Washington I will fight to guarantee that no one is left behind, no child denied care and no family bankrupted for the right to live.

priorities.text: Increasing public school funding, opposing the diversion of taxpayer dollars to private schools she says face little transparency or accountability.
priorities.quote: Public dollars belong in public schools, and I will fight in Washington to ensure Arizona invests in its students instead of subsidizing unregulated private institutions.

priorities.text: Addressing the housing affordability crisis by curbing corporate control of real estate.
priorities.quote: In Washington I will fight to curb corporate control of real estate and put the dream of safe, affordable housing back within reach for Arizona families.

positions.summary: Says healthcare is a human right and pledges to fight so that no patient is denied care or bankrupted by medical costs, drawing on her career as a reproductive-health nurse and patient advocate.
Opposes directing public education dollars to private schools, saying 'public dollars belong in public schools.'
positions.quote: Public dollars belong in public schools, and I will fight in Washington to ensure Arizona invests in its students instead of subsidizing unregulated private institutions.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to curb corporate control of the real-estate market to make housing more affordable for Arizona families.

candidates.name: Mark Lamb
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 58.6% of the vote, endorsed by President Trump

summary.text: Mark Lamb is the former Sheriff of Pinal County, Arizona (2017-2024) and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 5th Congressional District, an open seat. He was previously the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in 2024, losing the primary to Kari Lake. He received the endorsement of President Donald Trump and Turning Point USA in this race, and won his primary amid public allegations of sending sexually charged messages to multiple women, which he has disputed.

background.text: Born in Hawaii in 1972; graduated from Chandler High School in Arizona.
Worked for the police department of the Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community for six years before joining the Pinal County Sheriff's Office in 2012.
Elected Sheriff of Pinal County in 2016 and re-elected unopposed in 2020, serving from January 2017 to December 2024.
Co-founded Protect America Now, a coalition of sheriffs, in February 2021.
Ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 to succeed Kyrsten Sinema, and was defeated in the Republican primary by Kari Lake.

priorities.text: Campaigns on a platform of traditional values, describing a need for what news coverage characterized as a 'national revival of faith, family, freedom' and gun rights, while denouncing what he calls 'America's moral decay.'

positions.summary: Campaign platform includes support for gun rights as part of a broader 'faith, family, freedom' message.

record.text: Multiple women alleged, in public records verified by the Arizona Republic and KTAR News, that Lamb sent them sexually charged messages while sheriff; one woman said he threatened her with revenge-porn charges. Lamb did not deny specific claims but called many of the allegations baseless. In 2026, the Pinal County Attorney's Office reviewed the matter and found 'no evidence that Lamb acted in a criminal manner.'

The American Sheriff Foundation, a charity Lamb established in 2018, was reported by the Arizona Republic in 2020 to have left at least $18,000 in spending unaccounted for; the nonprofit lost its federal and state status and was dissolved in 2024 after Lamb acknowledged failing to comply with Arizona disclosure and reporting requirements.

researchNotes: Ballotpedia's page for Mark Lamb lacked a biography section and detailed 2026 issue coverage, so his background, the misconduct allegations, and the American Sheriff Foundation matter are drawn from Wikipedia, which in turn cites the Arizona Republic, AZ Luminaria, KTAR News, and Politico; those underlying news articles were not independently fetched within this research session's time budget. Lamb's campaign website did not render usable content in this environment (JavaScript-rendered), so his specific 2026 issue positions beyond general campaign-theme reporting could not be confirmed and most are left out per the research standard. Elizabeth Lee's positions are drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers.
